item.title: Modder Boots Googlebook OS on Apple Silicon Macs
item.description:
Googlebook laptops arrived only a few weeks ago, and Googlebook OS is already running on hardware Google never built it for. Developer Skylar Taylor-Barrick has published gbos-vm, an open-source project that boots the OS inside a GPU-accelerated virtual machine on Apple Silicon Macs, with Chrome working. Apparently, the install script downloads Google's own recovery image for the Dell XPS Googlebook, an ARM64 build based on Android 17, replaces the hardware-specific vendor partition with virtual device components from Google's Cuttlefish project, and boots it under QEMU.

The Dell is one of the Snapdragon X-powered Googlebooks, so its Arm image runs on the Mac's hypervisor without emulation. That also means Intel Macs are out. Googlebook OS renders through Vulkan while Macs use Metal, so the project passes Vulkan calls through MoltenVK. The README asks for 16 GB of RAM, 60 GB of free storage, Xcode command line tools, and the Android SDK with NDK, plus a hefty 9 GB of downloads. First boot takes about 45 seconds on an M5 MacBook, which is the only machine the developer lists as tested.

item.title: Ghost of Yotei Reaches Gameplay on PS5 Emulator SharpEmu, Performance Still Needs Work
item.description:
Ghost of Yotei has become the latest PlayStation 5 exclusive to get past its menus on PC. Developer Foued (@foufouadi_) shared footage on X of Sucker Punch's 2025 samurai game running in a modified build of SharpEmu, the experimental PS5 emulator whose playable list is mostly small indie and retro-style titles. The clip shows the start menu, a 3D environment loading in, and protagonist Atsu moving around. The results, however, are far from playable. Foued clarified that the video was sped up, and the real frame rate is reportedly around 1 to 2 FPS, with geometry and texture errors on top. Apparently, performance work will come later.

A separate screenshot shows the fight against The Snake, the game's first boss, at 10.9 FPS on a GeForce RTX 4090 and Ryzen 7 7800X3D, with some effects still rendering incorrectly. Another attempt through AnyPS5, which relinks PS5 executables instead of emulating the console, is further behind, with the game world reportedly loading at roughly 3.4 frames per minute. Ghost of Yotei follows Marvel's Wolverine, which booted on KytyPS5 late last month and has since reached around 20 FPS. The same emulator also ran the PS5 version of GTA 5 at up to 60 FPS. Interest in these projects picked up after Sony moved away from PC ports of its single-player games, with a planned Ghost of Yotei port reportedly among those scrapped. A playable build is still a long way off, though it's reasonable to expect quick improvements given how fast these emulators have moved.

item.title: Steam Tops 43.5 Million Concurrent Players, New All-Time High
item.description:
Sundays are designated as free time, and gamers are confirming that today, as Steam has reportedly hit 43.5 million concurrent players, representing a new all-time high. On Sunday, October 11, at exactly 14:00 UTC, 43.5 million gamers were online to chat, play, and enter their favorite digital worlds for entertainment. This marks a new all-time high for the platform, which has broken countless records in the past. Interestingly, one might expect this record to occur during the holiday season when most people have extra time to play. However, it seems that the number of gamers on Steam is increasing even during regular times. Several factors could be contributing to this, including gamers trying out new hardware purchased during the holiday season, seeking discounts, or simply browsing the platform to see if anything interesting is happening.

At the same time, the number of players in-game was recorded at 14.46 million active gamers, meaning the rest were using the platform to browse, chat, or perhaps do some game shopping. Nonetheless, 43.5 million concurrent Steam users is a massive achievement. With many new AAA game titles being released recently, alongside Steam being the platform of choice for publishing games, it is currently experiencing demand that keeps piling on. More platforms like the Steam Frame VR headset will also help boost that figure even higher, and as gamers are using all available devices to transform them into mini Steam Decks, the surge is expected. Let us know in the comments if you contributed with this weekend's surge, and with which game!

item.title: Microsoft Warns Windows Update Will Stop Working on Unpatched PCs Next Year
item.description:
Microsoft is replacing the certificates that Windows PCs use to confirm they are talking to genuine Windows Update servers, and machines that miss the changeover will stop receiving updates. The company announced the rotation on October 8, and the current certificates expire on May 17 and June 19, 2027. Most users apparently won't have to do anything, since the replacements ship inside the regular monthly security updates. Windows 11 25H2 and later, including the recently launched 26H2, need no action. Windows 11 24H2 needs the September 2025 security update or newer, while other supported Windows 11 and Windows 10 versions need the July 2026 update or later before June 19. Windows 10 Enterprise 2019 LTSC, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2016 face the earlier May 17 deadline.

Microsoft says devices on unsupported versions "will lose access to Windows Update services and won't receive any updates as a result," and its only advice is to upgrade. For home users, that mostly points at Windows 10 PCs that were never enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU) after the OS reached end of life in October 2025. Those machines probably never got the July 2026 patch. Microsoft extended ESU coverage to October 12, 2027, so it looks like enrolling and installing the offered updates before June should bring the new certificates along. The warning also comes months after Microsoft began refreshing Secure Boot certificates that were due to expire in late June 2026. Readers are advised to check their update history for a cumulative update from July 2026 or later.

item.title: Activision DMCA Takes Down Vibe-Coded Call of Duty Browser Ports
item.description:
Activision has reportedly issued a DMCA takedown against a set of unofficial Call of Duty browser ports made by developer Luckey Faraday. Faraday announced it on X, saying the publisher went after him "for porting CoD games to the browser," that every related post was removed, and that every game is now offline. He also asked whether he is the first "vibe coder" to get a DMCA notice from a major gaming company. The notice itself hasn't been shared publicly, so the exact claims are not known, and Activision doesn't seem to have commented so far. The projects in question are Claude of Duty: Vibe Slops II, a Black Ops 2 multiplayer recreation, and Kino der Toten, a browser version of Black Ops Zombies. Both ran on Three.js and were built with the help of AI coding agents.

Vibe Slops II offered free-for-all matches against six bots on Hijacked and Nuketown 2025, while the Zombies project had Kino der Toten fully playable solo. The project pages state that the maps, models, and animations were exported from the original PC games, which probably didn't help Faraday's case, even with both labeled as non-commercial fan projects. The Kino der Toten repository was still accessible on GitHub at the time of writing, so it looks like the takedown hit the hosted games and the posts promoting them. It comes less than two weeks after Take-Two sent a cease-and-desist to the modder behind the GTA 5 Switch port, and shortly after a free browser port of Halo: Combat Evolved showed up.

item.title: KINGPIN Says a Connector Dispute With NVIDIA Derailed EVGA's Last Flagship Card
item.description:
Vince "KINGPIN" Lucido has blamed NVIDIA for the troubled launch of the EVGA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti KINGPIN, the last graphics card to carry his name. In the first video on his new Overclocking Kingpin YouTube channel, the overclocker said he wanted the card to have two 12VHPWR power connectors, while NVIDIA wanted it limited to just one. The disagreement, in his words, "really screwed up the production timeline", and he also holds it responsible for how few units were made afterward. The card did eventually ship with both 16-pin connectors when it went on sale for $2,500 with a bundled 1600 W power supply, about three months after the RTX 3090 Ti itself came out. This is only Lucido's side of the story, and it isn't clear why NVIDIA pushed for a single connector.

In September 2022, EVGA ended its partnership with NVIDIA and stopped making graphics cards, with CEO Andrew Han pointing to a souring relationship between the two companies. Every card in development was canceled, KINGPIN models included. Lucido is now working with ASUS, which sent over the hardware shown in the video, although no ASUS-made KINGPIN card has been confirmed. He did lay out one condition for such a card: the PCB and power delivery have to let the GPU reach its full potential under liquid nitrogen without the buyer modifying anything. An earlier plan with PNY never produced a card, and Lucido ended up skipping the RTX 50 generation entirely.
